# Sirach Chapter 47 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 47 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**47:1** After him came Nathan to prophesy in David's time.

**47:2** Just as fat is skimmed from the peace offering, David was chosen out from among the children of Israel.

**47:3** He played with lions as if they were kittens and with bears as if they were lambs.

**47:4** In his youth, didn't he kill a giant and lift a disgrace from his people? He swung his arm with a single smooth stone and brought Goliath's bragging to a permanent end.

**47:5** He called on the Lord Most High, who put strength in his right arm to cut down a warrior and raise the horn of his people.

**47:6** So the women of Israel sang his praises — tens of thousands for David!

**47:7** When he strapped on armor and went to war, he drew his sword against the Philistines and his hand dealt with many of them.

**47:8** Before any undertaking, he would set his hands in the right direction — giving thanks to the Holy One Most High with words of glory.

**47:9** With his whole heart he sang praises and loved his Maker. He stationed singers before the altar, and their voices made the melody sweet.

**47:10** He added splendor to the festivals and arranged the seasons to run in perfect order through the year, while they praised the holy name and the sanctuary rang from morning to night.

**47:11** The Lord forgave his sins and raised his horn forever; he gave him a royal covenant and a throne of glory in Israel.

**47:12** After him came a wise son who found safety in his father's blessing.

**47:13** Solomon reigned in peaceful days. God gave him rest on every side, so that he could build a house for God's name and prepare an enduring sanctuary.

**47:14** What wisdom you had in your youth! You overflowed with understanding like a flooding river!

**47:15** Your mind ranged over the whole earth; you filled it with proverbs full of hidden meaning.

**47:16** Your name reached the farthest islands; you were loved for the peace you brought.

**47:17** Your songs, your proverbs, your parables, your wit — the whole world stood in awe of you.

**47:18** In the name of the Lord God, called the God of Israel, you gathered gold like tin and piled up silver like lead.

**47:19** But you gave yourself to women; they got the better of you bodily.

**47:20** You stained your glory and shamed your descendants, bringing wrath down on your children — and they suffered for your foolishness,

**47:21** when the kingdom split in two and a rebel state rose out of Ephraim.

**47:22** But the Lord will not abandon his mercy or let any of his words fail; he will not blot out the descendants of his chosen one or destroy the line of him who loved him; so he gave Jacob a remnant and David a root from his own stock.

**47:23** Solomon rested with his ancestors and left behind his offspring — Rehoboam, an empty-headed fool — who by his policies drove the people away. And then Jeroboam son of Nebat led Israel into sin and put Ephraim on the road to destruction.

**47:24** Their sins multiplied so enormously that they were finally expelled from their land.

**47:25** For they chased after every kind of wickedness until the day of reckoning arrived.
